content: 1. Immune checkpoint inhibitors may have their therapeutic effects reduced when co-administered with certain agents. Close monitoring is advised in such cases. 2. Azithromycin can reduce the efficacy of ampicillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is considered minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. 3. Ampicillin may decrease the effects of balstilimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 4. Co-administration of ampicillin with immune checkpoint inhibitors may interfere with their therapeutic effects. Close monitoring is necessary. 5. Ampicillin can reduce the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Ampicillin decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine (live) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is serious, and the live bacterial vaccine should not be administered until antibiotic therapy is complete. 7. Bendroflumethiazide increases the effects of ampicillin by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. It may increase side effects, so close monitoring is recommended. 8. Ampicillin reduces the effects of camrelizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 9. Ampicillin decreases the effects of cemiplimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 10. Chloramphenicol reduces the effects of ampicillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. 11. Chloroquine decreases the levels of ampicillin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Doses should be separated by at least 2 hours, and caution is advised. 12. Chlorothiazide increases the levels of ampicillin by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. 13. Ampicillin reduces the effects of the cholera vaccine (live) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration with systemic antibiotics should be avoided, as these agents may act against the vaccine strain. The cholera vaccine should not be administered to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 14. Ampicillin and choline magnesium trisalicylate can increase each other's levels by decreasing renal clearance or through plasma protein binding competition. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 15. Clarithromycin reduces the effects of ampicillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. 16. Colestipol decreases the levels of ampicillin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Its clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 17. Ampicillin reduces the effects of cosibelimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 18. Ampicillin and deflazacort both decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 19. Demeclocycline reduces the effects of ampicillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. Monitor for decreased therapeutic effects of penicillins if used concomitantly with tetracyclines. 20. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of ampicillin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 21. Didanosine decreases the levels or effects of ampicillin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Its clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 22. Ampicillin reduces the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. An alternative or additional form of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. 23. Ampicillin decreases the effects of dostarlimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 24. Doxycycline reduces the effects of ampicillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. Monitor for decreased therapeutic effects of penicillins if used concomitantly with tetracyclines. 25. Ampicillin decreases the effects of durvalumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 26. Eravacycline reduces the effects of ampicillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. Monitor for decreased therapeutic effects of penicillins if used concomitantly with tetracyclines. 27. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) reduces the effects of ampicillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. These interactions are minor, but their clinical significance is unknown. 28. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of ampicillin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 29. Ampicillin reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Hydrochlorothiazide increases the levels of ampicillin by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. 31. Ibuprofen/famotidine decreases the levels or effects of ampicillin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 32. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of ampicillin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 33. Lanthanum carbonate decreases the levels of ampicillin by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Ampicillin should be administered at least 2 hours before or after lanthanum. This interaction applies to oral ampicillin. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 34. Ampicillin reduces the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 35. Ampicillin reduces the levels or effects of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 36. Ampicillin increases the levels of methotrexate by decreasing renal clearance. Increased serum concentrations of methotrexate with concomitant hematologic and gastrointestinal toxicity have been observed with concurrent administration of high or low doses of methotrexate and penicillins. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 37. Methyclothiazide increases the levels of ampicillin by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. 38. Metolazone increases the levels of ampicillin by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. 39. Ampicillin reduces the effects of oral microbiota by pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. Antibacterial agents may decrease efficacy if co-administered. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota. 40. Minocycline reduces the effects of ampicillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. Monitor for decreased therapeutic effects of penicillins if used concomitantly with tetracyclines. 41. Ampicillin and mycophenolate can increase each other's levels by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. 42. Ampicillin decreases the effects of nivolumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 43. Omadacycline reduces the effects of ampicillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. Monitor for decreased therapeutic effects of penicillins if used concomitantly with tetracyclines. 44. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of ampicillin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 45. Oxytetracycline reduces the effects of ampicillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. 46. Pantoprazole decreases the levels or effects of ampicillin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 47. Ampicillin decreases the effects of pembrolizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 48. Ampicillin decreases the effects of penpulimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 49. Rabeprazole decreases the levels or effects of ampicillin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 50. Ampicillin decreases the effects of retifanlimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 51. Rifampin decreases the levels of ampicillin by increasing metabolism. This interaction is minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. 52. Ampicillin and rose hips can increase each other's levels by decreasing renal clearance. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 53. Roxithromycin reduces the effects of ampicillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. 54. Sarecycline reduces the effects of ampicillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. 55. Ampicillin decreases the effects of sintilimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 56. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels or effects of ampicillin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 57. Sodium citrate/citric acid decreases the levels or effects of ampicillin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 58. Ampicillin and sodium phenylacetate can increase each other's levels by decreasing renal clearance. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 59. Ampicillin decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Co-administration with antibiotics decreases efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 60. Ampicillin and sodium sulfate/potassium chloride/magnesium sulfate/polyethylene glycol both decrease serum potassium. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 61. Ampicillin increases the effects of spironolactone through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Hyperkalemia may occur, so caution and close monitoring are necessary. 62. Ampicillin and sulfasalazine can increase each other's levels by plasma protein binding competition or by decreasing renal clearance. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 63. Tetracycline reduces the effects of ampicillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. 64. Ampicillin decreases the effects of tislelizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 65. Ampicillin decreases the effects of toripalimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 66. Ampicillin decreases the effects of the typhoid vaccine (live) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is contraindicated, and the live bacterial vaccine should not be administered until antibiotic therapy is complete. 67. Ampicillin and willow bark can increase each other's levels by decreasing renal clearance. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 68. Ampicillin may cause various adverse effects, including erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, rash, urticaria, fever, seizures, black hairy tongue, diarrhea, enterocolitis, glossitis, nausea, oral candidiasis, pseudomembranous colitis, stomatitis, vomiting, agranulocytosis, anemia, hemolytic anemia, eosinophilia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, purpura, anaphylaxis, increased aspartate aminotransferase, interstitial nephritis, laryngeal stridor, serum sickness-like reactions, and hypersensitivity. 69. Use caution in patients with allergies to cephalosporins or carbapenems. Adjust the dose in renal failure and evaluate rashes to differentiate from hypersensitivity reactions. 70. Ampicillin is associated with a high incidence of rash in patients with infectious mononucleosis. Avoid therapy in these patients. 71. Prolonged use of ampicillin may lead to fungal or bacterial superinfection. 72. Ampicillin is excreted in breast milk; use caution during lactation. 73. Ampicillin is generally considered safe during pregnancy (Category B). Controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk. 74. Ampicillin is primarily excreted in the urine, with 90% eliminated within 24 hours.
